relations.note: Aten was formulated through Re and retained Re in both didactic names.
The early didactic name explicitly incorporated Re-Horakhty into Aten's identity.
Re-Horakhty's name was removed when Aten's titulary became more exclusive.
Aten existed in Shu's name, possibly identifying Shu with the disc's radiance.
Shu's explicit divine name disappeared from Aten's revised titulary.
Horus was indirectly present through Horakhty in Aten's early titulary.
Aten's order was associated with Maat, though she was neither consort nor daughter.
Amun's names and images were attacked while Aten's institutions displaced his cult.

relations.myth: Displacement of the Theban divine household
relations.note: Mut's cult was affected by Atenist attacks on Amun's divine household.
Khonsu was institutionally displaced with the Theban triad under exclusive Atenism.
Atenist exclusivity marginalized Ptah's cult without making him a mythic opponent.
Official Amarna tombs largely omitted Osirian imagery and postmortem judgment.

relations.note: Hathoric features in Nefertiti's imagery indirectly supplied Aten worship a female solar complement.
Bes remained present on domestic objects at Amarna alongside the official Aten cult.
Taweret remained present on domestic objects at Amarna alongside the official Aten cult.
Some scholars identify the deified, solarized king with Aten, but ancient texts do not.
Aten was Akhenaten's divine father in royal theology, not conventional genealogy.
